risk.going_concern: Official doubt about the company's ability to keep operating
risk.sub_dollar: Price below the listing floor, {n} sessions in a row
risk.tip.going_concern: In their official report, the auditor writes that they doubt the company will survive twelve months: it is the most direct accounting signal of distress there is.
risk.tip.reverse_split: The company reduced the number of shares outstanding to mechanically lift its price — most often in order to stay listed.
risk.tip.dilution: A document preparing an issuance of new shares has been filed: your stake will be reduced. Read it against the line of business — a company with no revenue yet funds itself this way as a matter of course, so the fact is frequent there and does not say the same thing as elsewhere.
risk.tip.late_filing: The quarterly or annual report was not filed on time and the company declared it: internal disorder, or disagreement with the auditor.
risk.tip.sub_dollar: The price stayed below the floor required by the listing venue for several sessions in a row. Past a certain duration, the company receives a non-compliance notice.
alerts.title: Alerts after earnings releases
alerts.empty: No alert in the journal yet.
alerts.intro: An alert is sent when a company reports quarterly earnings well above those of the same quarter a year earlier, scaled by the usual variability of its results (seasonal surprise, top quintile). Risk flags are information: they remove no alert.
alerts.today.title: Today's releases
alerts.today.empty: No release in the top quintile for the session of {d}.
alerts.journal.title: Journal
stats.title: Average realized return by horizon
stats.realized.def: Realized return: simple, gross return from the open of the entry day to the close of the horizon session, prices adjusted for splits and dividends; IWM (US small-cap index fund) over the same dates.
stats.missing.def: "No price": the horizon session has passed and no price exists for the stock (delisted or trading halted). These alerts are counted separately: they are not in the average.
net.def: A measure of a different kind from the realized return: logarithmic gap to stocks of the same size and volatility on the same day, net of the cost of the gap between buy and sell prices (spread). The two figures are not directly comparable.
